description: Byte known-answer tests for ak.schema.approval_signature.v1 (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2). Every signature here is a real Ed25519 signature made with the published conformance fixture key, so a verifier reproduces the accepted vectors and refutes the rejected ones without trusting this fixture's prose. The target Event's digest preimage, event_digest and derived event_id are the ones content-bound-event-id-fixture.json already fixes, which is what makes the event_id-invariance claim checkable rather than asserted.

vectors.name: ak.vector.authz.approval_signature_bytes.v1
vectors.description: Grant-context approval over an already authored Event: the canonical branch of zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2. request_canonical_digest covers the complete Event including its producer proof.

test_private_key_jwk.note: Public conformance test key only: the private key ships with the specification, so a valid signature over it proves nothing about the signer. Registered in artifacts/registry/test-material-registry.json; formal verification, authorization and trust-admission paths MUST refuse it and the reserved identifiers it uses. See zh/identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 8.

expected.original_input: complete authored Event including its producer proof

vectors.name: ak.vector.authz.approval_signature_governance_context.v1
vectors.description: Realm-governance-context approval over the same Event. The branch carries no grant_id and no governance configuration identifier: realm_id, action and approval_target already determine the requirement (zh/models/governance-objects.md section 3.5).

test_private_key_jwk.note: Public conformance test key only: the private key ships with the specification, so a valid signature over it proves nothing about the signer. Registered in artifacts/registry/test-material-registry.json; formal verification, authorization and trust-admission paths MUST refuse it and the reserved identifiers it uses. See zh/identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 8.

expected.original_input: complete authored Event including its producer proof

vectors.name: ak.vector.authz.approval_signature_operation_target.v1
vectors.description: Grant-context approval over a non-Event operation target: request_canonical_digest covers the original typed RequestBody of the registered operation ak.self.agent.command.renew_pairing.v1 and nothing else. This vector fixes the byte derivation only: v1 registers no evidence carrier on any non-Event operation, so no operation may claim to support the workflow (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.5).

test_private_key_jwk.note: Public conformance test key only: the private key ships with the specification, so a valid signature over it proves nothing about the signer. Registered in artifacts/registry/test-material-registry.json; formal verification, authorization and trust-admission paths MUST refuse it and the reserved identifiers it uses. See zh/identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 8.

expected.original_input: original typed RequestBody of the registered operation

event_id_invariance.description: Attaching approval_signatures[] to EventCommitSubmission MUST NOT change the Event. The Event digest preimage omits event_id, proofs and unsigned, and the evidence is not an Event member at all, so both the preimage bytes and the derived id are byte-identical before and after. The HTTP Content-Digest over the transmitted body does change, which is why zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.3 calls the two checks independent.

negative_cases.name: reject_substituted_request_canonical_digest
negative_cases.description: The approved Event body is replaced by another one: request_canonical_digest no longer names the bytes that were approved, so the retained signature does not verify.

expected.reason: The approved Event body is replaced by another one: request_canonical_digest no longer names the bytes that were approved, so the retained signature does not verify.

negative_cases.name: reject_substituted_event_id
negative_cases.description: approval_target.event_id is repointed at a different Event. An approval is bound to one exact target, so it MUST NOT travel to another Event.

expected.reason: approval_target.event_id is repointed at a different Event. An approval is bound to one exact target, so it MUST NOT travel to another Event.

negative_cases.name: reject_substituted_realm_id
negative_cases.description: realm_id is replaced: cross-Realm replay of one approval MUST fail.

expected.reason: realm_id is replaced: cross-Realm replay of one approval MUST fail.

negative_cases.name: reject_substituted_action
negative_cases.description: action is replaced by another registered capability action: one approval does not authorize a different action.

expected.reason: action is replaced by another registered capability action: one approval does not authorize a different action.

negative_cases.name: reject_substituted_operation
negative_cases.description: operation is replaced by another registered entry point: the same action replayed through another operation MUST fail (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.4).

expected.reason: operation is replaced by another registered entry point: the same action replayed through another operation MUST fail (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.4).

negative_cases.name: reject_substituted_initiating_actor_station
negative_cases.description: initiating_actor_id keeps principal_id and changes station_id only. Accounts with the same principal at different Stations are permanently distinct, so the approval MUST NOT carry over.

expected.reason: initiating_actor_id keeps principal_id and changes station_id only. Accounts with the same principal at different Stations are permanently distinct, so the approval MUST NOT carry over.

negative_cases.name: reject_substituted_grant_id
negative_cases.description: approval_context.grant_id is repointed at another grant: a grant-context approval is evidence for one specific grant's requirement.

expected.reason: approval_context.grant_id is repointed at another grant: a grant-context approval is evidence for one specific grant's requirement.

negative_cases.name: reject_substituted_approval_context_branch
negative_cases.description: The grant branch is rewritten as the realm_governance branch to reuse one signature across both approval layers. The context is inside the signed input, so the swap MUST fail; a governance-context vote requires its own signature.

expected.reason: The grant branch is rewritten as the realm_governance branch to reuse one signature across both approval layers. The context is inside the signed input, so the swap MUST fail; a governance-context vote requires its own signature.

negative_cases.name: reject_substituted_nonce
negative_cases.description: nonce is replaced while the signature is kept, the shape a collector would try after learning that the original nonce was consumed.

expected.reason: nonce is replaced while the signature is kept, the shape a collector would try after learning that the original nonce was consumed.

negative_cases.name: reject_substituted_approved_at
negative_cases.description: approved_at is moved to bring an out-of-window approval back inside the window. The instant is signed, so it cannot be adjusted after the fact.

expected.reason: approved_at is moved to bring an out-of-window approval back inside the window. The instant is signed, so it cannot be adjusted after the fact.

negative_cases.name: reject_substituted_approver_did
negative_cases.description: approver_did is replaced to credit the vote to another approver while keeping the signature.

expected.reason: approver_did is replaced to credit the vote to another approver while keeping the signature.

negative_cases.name: reject_operation_target_digest_substituted
negative_cases.description: The operation branch's original typed RequestBody is replaced, so request_canonical_digest no longer covers the approved body.

expected.reason: The operation branch's original typed RequestBody is replaced, so request_canonical_digest no longer covers the approved body.

negative_cases.name: reject_signature_over_input_without_domain_prefix
negative_cases.description: A real signature over JCS(input) with the domain prefix omitted. The prefix is what separates this domain from every other signature the same key makes, so an implementation that drops it MUST NOT be accepted even though its signature verifies over its own bytes.

expected.reason: signing_bytes MUST begin with UTF8(ak.approval.signature.v1) || 0x0A

negative_cases.name: reject_signature_over_a_digest_of_the_input
negative_cases.description: A real signature over SHA-256(JCS(input)) instead of over signing_bytes. zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.1 registers the signing input itself as the primitive and forbids the digest-then-sign shape, so this MUST fail closed rather than be accepted as an equivalent construction.

expected.reason: the registered primitive is the signing input, never a digest of it

negative_cases.name: reject_producer_proof_jws_presented_as_approval_proof
negative_cases.description: The Event's own producer proof, made with the same key, is presented as the approval proof. Both signatures are genuine and the key resolves, yet the domains differ, so the producer proof MUST NOT count as an approval. This is the cross-domain case one published key makes testable.

expected.reason: a proof from another signing domain is not an approval signature

negative_cases.name: reject_flipped_signature_bit
negative_cases.description: One bit of the Ed25519 signature is flipped; every other byte of the vector is unchanged.

expected.reason: signature bytes do not verify over signing_bytes

negative_cases.name: reject_non_empty_jws_payload_segment
negative_cases.description: The attached compact form carries signing_bytes in the payload segment. The detached profile requires an empty middle segment even when the attached form would verify.

expected.reason: detached_jws payload segment MUST be empty in compact serialization

negative_cases.name: reject_substituted_verification_method
negative_cases.description: verification_method is repointed at another key of the same approver DID. The member is not signed and carries no authority: it only selects a key, so substituting it yields an invalid signature rather than a second valid reading.

expected.reason: the selected key is not the key that produced this signature

negative_cases.name: reject_missing_input_member
negative_cases.description: nonce is absent. input is a closed object whose ten members are all required, so a missing member is schema_violation and MUST NOT be reported as signature_invalid (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.5 reducer rule 1).

expected.reason: nonce is absent. input is a closed object whose ten members are all required, so a missing member is schema_violation and MUST NOT be reported as signature_invalid (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.5 reducer rule 1).

negative_cases.name: reject_null_filled_absent_member
negative_cases.description: nonce is present as null. An absent member MUST NOT be reconstructed as null or as a local default; the object is still schema-invalid.

expected.reason: nonce is present as null. An absent member MUST NOT be reconstructed as null or as a local default; the object is still schema-invalid.

negative_cases.name: reject_extra_input_member
negative_cases.description: An unregistered member is added to input. The object is closed, so an extra member is schema_violation rather than an ignorable extension.

expected.reason: An unregistered member is added to input. The object is closed, so an extra member is schema_violation rather than an ignorable extension.

negative_cases.name: reject_proof_inside_input
negative_cases.description: The proof object is nested inside input. proof MUST NOT be a member of input: nothing outside input is covered by the signature, and a self-covering input has no fixed point.

expected.reason: The proof object is nested inside input. proof MUST NOT be a member of input: nothing outside input is covered by the signature, and a self-covering input has no fixed point.

negative_cases.name: reject_governance_context_carrying_grant_id
negative_cases.description: The realm_governance branch carries a grant_id. The branch is closed and an implementation MUST NOT fabricate a grant_id to satisfy the schema.

expected.reason: The realm_governance branch carries a grant_id. The branch is closed and an implementation MUST NOT fabricate a grant_id to satisfy the schema.

negative_cases.name: reject_governance_context_carrying_governance_configuration_reference
negative_cases.description: The realm_governance branch carries a digest of the Realm's governance configuration. A private governance reference MUST NOT ride along in evidence that may leave the Station: realm_id, action and approval_target already determine the requirement, and the branch is closed so there is nowhere to put one.

expected.reason: The realm_governance branch carries a digest of the Realm's governance configuration. A private governance reference MUST NOT ride along in evidence that may leave the Station: realm_id, action and approval_target already determine the requirement, and the branch is closed so there is nowhere to put one.

negative_cases.name: reject_event_target_without_event_id
negative_cases.description: The event branch omits event_id, leaving request_canonical_digest as the only binding. The branch is closed and requires the exact target id.

expected.reason: The event branch omits event_id, leaving request_canonical_digest as the only binding. The branch is closed and requires the exact target id.

negative_cases.name: reject_operation_target_carrying_event_id
negative_cases.description: The operation branch carries an event_id. The two target branches are a closed XOR and MUST remain decidable from the schema alone.

expected.reason: The operation branch carries an event_id. The two target branches are a closed XOR and MUST remain decidable from the schema alone.

negative_cases.name: reject_unregistered_operation_token
negative_cases.description: operation names a token that operation-registry.json does not list. It satisfies the member's syntactic pattern, so the closed schema alone cannot refute it: the registry does, and the outcome is still schema_violation rather than an unknown-entry-point runtime error.

expected.reason: operation names a token that operation-registry.json does not list. It satisfies the member's syntactic pattern, so the closed schema alone cannot refute it: the registry does, and the outcome is still schema_violation rather than an unknown-entry-point runtime error.

negative_cases.name: reject_short_nonce
negative_cases.description: nonce is shorter than the registered minimum, so it cannot carry 128 bits of entropy.

expected.reason: nonce is shorter than the registered minimum, so it cannot carry 128 bits of entropy.

negative_cases.name: reject_present_and_empty_approval_signatures
negative_cases.description: EventCommitSubmission.approval_signatures is present and empty. The array is omitted when no approval layer demands evidence; present-and-empty is a distinct, forbidden third state (minItems 1).

expected.reason: approval_signatures MUST NOT be present and empty

negative_cases.name: reject_event_id_not_equal_to_submitted_event
negative_cases.description: A signature that verifies over its own bytes, whose approval_target.event_id names an Event other than the one in this submission. Reducer rule 3 requires the two to be equal, so the requirement stays unmet.

expected.reason: approval_target.event_id MUST equal the submitted Event's event_id

negative_cases.name: reject_nonce_reused_on_another_target
negative_cases.description: The (approval_context, approver_did, nonce) triple of an already accepted target is presented for a different target. An exact replay of the accepted target returns the original outcome; a different target MUST NOT.

expected.reason: the nonce was consumed by the accepted target and is not transferable

negative_cases.name: reject_approved_at_beyond_hard_future_skew
negative_cases.description: approved_at is later than the verification time plus the protocol-level hard_future_skew_ms. The signature verifies; the vote is still inadmissible, and an implementation MUST NOT widen the tolerance to accept it.

expected.reason: approved_at MUST NOT exceed the verification time plus hard_future_skew_ms

negative_cases.name: reject_approved_at_before_grant_issued_at
negative_cases.description: A grant-context approval signed before the grant it cites existed. The lower bound is the grant's issued_at, plus the not_before of its temporal grant-constraint when it carries one; a capability grant has no top-level not_before of its own.

expected.reason: approved_at precedes the grant's issued_at and its temporal not_before

negative_cases.name: reject_repeated_approver_counted_twice
negative_cases.description: Two distinct, individually valid signatures from the same approver_did, each with its own nonce, presented against a threshold of two. Both verify; they are one approver, so the quorum is not reached and neither nonce is consumed.

expected.reason: one approver casts one vote however many signatures it presents

negative_cases.name: reject_reused_votes_after_timeout
negative_cases.description: After the constraint's timeout expires, signatures collected under the old window are presented again. Every approval that had not reached the threshold is void: the approver MUST re-sign with a fresh nonce (reducer rule 5).

expected.reason: votes that never reached the threshold do not survive the timeout

negative_cases.name: reject_agent_confirmation_counted_as_approval
negative_cases.description: An accepted ak.agent.action_approve Event is offered in place of an approval signature. It is a different object with a different nonce namespace and satisfies only the Agent draft publication gate; it MUST NOT be converted into a vote (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.6).

expected.reason: agent confirmation is not approval evidence for the target Event
